records.label: Indispensable amino-acid supply
records.limitation: Protein-quality scoring and vegetarian-diet amino-acid coverage do not establish that increasing protein raises brain monoamine synthesis or improves attention or mood. The indispensable set includes phenylalanine; tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.

records.label: Tyrosine
records.limitation: Dietary supply to a circulating pool is distinct from brain transport, catecholamine synthesis or clinical benefit. A small human study found higher plasma tyrosine during protein-containing meals and after a large tyrosine supplement; it does not define ordinary-food efficacy or a need for extra tyrosine when supply is adequate. Tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.

records.label: Tyrosine
records.limitation: Competitive transport biology does not establish that eating more tyrosine increases brain tyrosine or catecholamine signalling.

records.label: Tyrosine
records.limitation: Substrate necessity does not establish that additional dietary tyrosine increases brain dopamine or improves a functional or clinical outcome.

records.label: Tyrosine
records.limitation: Tyrosine is upstream precursor supply, not the immediate DBH substrate or an independently adjudicated Direct dietary requirement here. Ordinary dietary competitive changes do not establish a limiting effect on regional noradrenergic signalling or benefit from extra tyrosine.

records.label: Tryptophan

records.label: Tryptophan

records.label: Tryptophan

records.label: Egg-yolk phospholipid versus choline bitartrate

Faecal-consistency changes reported more often with phospholipid drink; not long-term tolerability evidence. Plasma concentration/iAUC is not measured absorption fraction, brain choline, acetylcholine synthesis or cognition. 37 g isolated egg phospholipids in a defined drink, not37 g egg yolk; whole-food equivalence untested. Specific causal mediator unresolved; omit a collapsed mechanism summary pending adequate identification.

records.label: Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)
records.limitation: This is a preclinical structural state response, not proof of an indispensable intake or verified new synapse counts. It does not establish human synapse growth, ordinary-food equivalence or cognitive benefit. Developmental mouse marker and visual-response evidence is additional, context-specific support; marker abundance is not an ultrastructurally verified contact count.

records.label: Tested fish-meal versus fish-oil capsule regimens over 16 weeks
records.limitation: Red-cell DHA is peripheral exposure, not neuronal incorporation, cognition or clinical benefit. No detected DHA group difference; nonsignificance is not equivalence. Post-hoc power could not detect RBC EPA+DHA differences below1.5 percentage points. Small unblinded active-comparator study without untreated control; fish adherence self-reported and groups differed in age. Specified albacore tuna, farmed Atlantic salmon and tested DHA-rich capsules; not arbitrary fish/capsule interchangeability. More fishy aftertaste with capsules; lipid changes do not establish cardiovascular benefit.

records.label: Methionine

In the cysteine-free study, methionine intake stayed adequate and red-cell synthesis did not fall. This does not show that eating more methionine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis.

records.label: Methionine

records.label: Potassium

records.label: Vitamin B6

records.label: Vitamin B6
records.limitation: Salvage of food vitamin B6 to pyridoxal 5'-phosphate does not show that higher vitamin B6 intake increases cystathionine beta-synthase or cystathionine gamma-lyase flux. records.label: Glycine
records.limitation: Endogenous glycine synthesis and other methyltransferases also contribute. Enzyme loss is not glycine deficiency; extra dietary glycine has not been established to normalise whole-cycle or brain methylation.

records.label: Glycine
records.limitation: In older adults glycine was supplemented together with a cysteine precursor, so that rise in erythrocyte synthesis does not isolate glycine.

records.label: Pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP; active vitamin B6 cofactor)
records.limitation: Purified-enzyme dependence on pyridoxal 5'-phosphate does not show that raising vitamin B6 intake increases cysteine formation in people. Moderate B6 restriction changed cystathionine handling but did not significantly reduce total transsulfuration in the assessed human tracer study.

records.label: Serine
records.limitation: Serine is a direct enzyme substrate. Endogenous synthesis and diet can both supply it; this does not show that dietary serine or protein intake increases cystathionine formation.

records.label: Cysteine
records.limitation: Cysteine is the substrate of the first assembly step. A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, and that formula also removed methionine. When methionine intake stayed adequate, removing cysteine did not lower red-cell synthesis in young men. This does not show that eating more cysteine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis.

records.label: Glutamate
records.limitation: No human study in this assessment showed that changing dietary glutamate changes glutathione synthesis.

records.label: N-acetylcysteine
records.limitation: The synthesis increase was measured in older adults given this precursor together with glycine. It does not show an effect of N-acetylcysteine alone, of ordinary foods, or of supplementation outside that group, and it is not a neuronal or clinical result.

records.label: Phosphatidylethanolamine
records.limitation: This identifies the phospholipid substrate of the reaction. It does not show that eating phosphatidylethanolamine or ethanolamine increases hepatic PEMT activity in humans.

records.label: S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe)
records.limitation: SAMe is made for this reaction by methionine adenosyltransferase. Needing SAMe as a substrate does not make SAMe supplements a requirement of the methylation, and it does not show that raising SAMe intake increases PEMT activity in humans.

records.label: Phosphatidylcholine
records.limitation: Plasma tracing does not measure absolute hepatic flux, intermediary SAM, ordinary-food equivalence or benefit.

records.label: Uridine
records.limitation: Uridine is a supported precursor source, not an indispensable dietary requirement: endogenous nucleotide synthesis and salvage also supply CTP. Rat-slice and oral-UMP gerbil results do not establish an ordinary-food dose, increased human PC flux or cognitive benefit; human MRS measures precursor pools.

records.label: Magnesium ions (Mg²⁺)
records.limitation: Reviewed UniProt IKBKB records the ATP-dependent IκB kinase reaction without a magnesium cofactor annotation; published IKKβ crystals used in this review are inhibitor-bound rather than ATP–Mg ternary complexes. This does not establish that ordinary dietary magnesium intake limits human NF-κB transcription.

records.label: Cysteine
records.limitation: This is supported upstream supply, not a demonstrated dietary constraint on NF-κB. Human precursor supplementation measured red-cell glutathione, not NF-κB; cysteine was supplied as N-acetylcysteine together with glycine. Cellular redox studies show context-dependent effects, including inhibition after glutathione depletion or increased extracellular cysteine. Neither individual dietary limitation, brain transfer nor benefit from additional intake is established.

records.label: Cysteine
records.limitation: Supported upstream supply through glutathione-dependent epithelial redox protection, not an established dietary constraint on endotoxin spillover. Human precursor tracing measured red-cell glutathione after combined glycine and N-acetylcysteine; epithelial experiments measured oxidant-induced paracellular permeability. In Salmonella-infected rats, glutathione depletion did not increase permeability or bacterial translocation. Neither intestinal precursor inadequacy, individual constituent limitation, human LPS reduction nor benefit from additional intake is established.

records.label: Glycine
records.limitation: This is supported upstream supply, not a demonstrated dietary constraint on NF-κB. Human precursor supplementation measured red-cell glutathione, not NF-κB; cysteine was supplied as N-acetylcysteine together with glycine. Cellular redox studies show context-dependent effects, including inhibition after glutathione depletion or increased extracellular cysteine. Neither individual dietary limitation, brain transfer nor benefit from additional intake is established.

records.label: Glycine
records.limitation: Supported upstream supply through glutathione-dependent epithelial redox protection, not an established dietary constraint on endotoxin spillover. Human precursor tracing measured red-cell glutathione after combined glycine and N-acetylcysteine; epithelial experiments measured oxidant-induced paracellular permeability. In Salmonella-infected rats, glutathione depletion did not increase permeability or bacterial translocation. Neither intestinal precursor inadequacy, individual constituent limitation, human LPS reduction nor benefit from additional intake is established.

records.label: Oligofructose
records.limitation: Defined 10% w/w mouse feeding is not a human dose or an ordinary-food effect. This is state regulation, not indispensability. Oligofructose is not chemically converted into GLP-2; no isolated butyrate mediation, generic fibre effect or brain benefit is established.

records.label: Sulforaphane
records.limitation: Human target engagement varies by formulation, tissue and population. The positive study used a myrosinase-completed broccoli sprout homogenate for three days in healthy nonsmokers and measured nasal phase II enzyme RNA, not Nrf2 protein or nuclear translocation. Extract capsules did not increase lung target-gene expression in COPD. An ordinary broccoli meal, direct activation of Nrf2 in the human brain and clinical ADHD benefit remain unestablished. Sulforaphane is not an essential nutrient.

records.label: Selenium
records.limitation: In selenium-deficient adults, plasma glutathione peroxidase activity levelled off once intake reached about 35 micrograms a day. Intake above that plateau did not raise the enzyme further, and the study did not measure net oxidative pressure.

records.label: Selenium
records.limitation: Mouse whole-organ enzyme assays do not identify mitochondrial isoforms, a human food dose or benefit above selenium adequacy. Repletion response depended on dose; antioxidant capacity does not establish clinical prevention.

records.label: Selenium
records.limitation: Culture selenium exposure is not an oral food dose. This supports the thioredoxin arm, not selenium dependence of glutathione reductase, universal tissue recycling flux or benefit above adequacy.

records.label: Zinc
records.limitation: Curated human SOD1 and experimental structural evidence support a structural capacity relationship, not zinc-dependent catalysis identical to copper. Human dietary SOD responses vary by isoform and status; extra zinc can disturb copper availability. No general oxidative-stress improvement or benefit above adequacy is established.

records.label: Copper
records.limitation: Erythrocyte superoxide dismutase rose after copper repletion in infants with marginal copper status. That does not show that extra copper raises the enzyme when status is already adequate.

records.label: Manganese
records.limitation: Human SOD2 requires manganese; dietary depletion experiments measured lower heart and kidney MnSOD activity in rats. This establishes a bounded enzyme-capacity dependency, not a human dose recommendation, universal tissue response, measured net ROS balance or benefit above adequate intake.

records.label: Glutathione
records.limitation: Glutathione is made in the body and used by the peroxidase. That is not evidence for eating glutathione.

records.label: Iron
records.limitation: Rat diet and tissue context; the kidney result is not a uniform response across organs or a human intake threshold. Human catalase haem identity supports capacity, not benefit from extra iron. Iron can also promote non-enzymatic oxidation; higher catalase activity is not a clinical benefit.

records.label: Vitamin E
records.limitation: Vitamin E breaks peroxyl-radical chains in membranes. That chemistry does not show that extra vitamin E lowers peroxidation in people. A prevention trial found more prostate cancers with 400 IU a day.

records.label: Vitamin E
records.limitation: Regeneration of the vitamin E radical is not a high-dose rule. A prevention trial found more prostate cancers with 400 IU of vitamin E a day.

records.label: Vitamin C supplementation and vitamin E retention
records.limitation: No significant change in nonsmoker disappearance, tocopherol maximal concentration/time-to-maximum, or F2-isoprostanes in either group. Small smoker-specific response; no general population supplementation rule. Retention cannot establish reduced oxidative injury or clinical benefit. Low-ascorbate diet and 17-day supplementation with day-14 tracer challenge; not a recommendation to restrict vitamin C or to offset smoking harms.

records.label: Vitamin C
records.limitation: Pulse radiolysis shows ascorbate reacting with the vitamin E radical. It does not show that more vitamin C speeds recycling in people.

records.label: Vitamin C supplementation and vitamin E retention
records.limitation: No significant change in nonsmoker disappearance, tocopherol maximal concentration/time-to-maximum, or F2-isoprostanes in either group. Small smoker-specific response; no general population supplementation rule. Retention cannot establish reduced oxidative injury or clinical benefit. Low-ascorbate diet and 17-day supplementation with day-14 tracer challenge; not a recommendation to restrict vitamin C or to offset smoking harms.

records.label: Vitamin B2
records.limitation: Human red-cell enzyme evidence supports flavin-dependent capacity. It does not establish neuronal or whole-body recycling flux, benefit above adequacy, or equivalence between an ordinary food and a 5 mg/day supplement.

records.label: Flavin adenine dinucleotide
records.limitation: Reaction participation does not establish oral FAD delivery, a food FAD concentration or additional-intake benefit.

records.label: DHA (Docosahexaenoic Acid)
records.limitation: Fifteen male soccer players, eight weeks, 1.16 g DHA/day in a matched beverage comparison. Ex-vivo stimulated production is not resting circulating signalling, receptor response or universal anti-inflammatory benefit. No effect from ordinary fish portions or brain/ADHD outcome is established; temperature and exercise responses differ.

records.label: DHA
records.limitation: Five days of 2.4 g a day in healthy adults raised some pro-resolving mediators, not every mediator, and not a disease-resolution outcome.

records.label: EPA
records.limitation: Five days of 2.4 g a day in healthy adults raised some pro-resolving mediators, not every mediator, and not a disease-resolution outcome.

records.label: Iron
records.limitation: This identifies iron centres in the chain. It does not show that eating more iron, once iron status is adequate, raises electron transport.

records.label: Iron
records.limitation: Capacity admission only: no CoQ-specific intake target, rate limitation under adequate nutrition, increased synthesis from extra intake, mitochondrial delivery or clinical benefit is established.

records.label: Flavin mononucleotide (FMN)
records.limitation: The review identifies the cofactor. It does not show that flavin mononucleotide (FMN) supply limits complex I in ordinary life, or that raising intake increases electron transport.

records.label: Vitamin B2 (riboflavin)
records.limitation: The review does not show that eating more riboflavin, once flavin mononucleotide (FMN) is adequate, raises electron transport. Riboflavin-responsive complex I disease is a separate clinical context.

records.label: Vitamin B2
records.limitation: Capacity admission only: no CoQ-specific intake target, rate limitation under adequate nutrition, increased synthesis from extra intake, mitochondrial delivery or clinical benefit is established.

records.label: Copper
records.limitation: Specific complex-IV metal dependence and dietary-deficiency evidence support capacity supply. Rat cardiac protein/activity effects are not a human optimisation dose, a universal tissue response or proof that extra copper improves electron transport when status is adequate.

records.label: Copper
records.limitation: Legacy record preserved. This assessment did not establish PM4-specific dietary engagement; general clearance roles are not imported.

records.label: Tyrosine
records.limitation: Capacity admission only: no CoQ-specific intake target, rate limitation under adequate nutrition, increased synthesis from extra intake, mitochondrial delivery or clinical benefit is established. Endogenous phenylalanine conversion is an alternative source; the full human intervening enzyme sequence remains incompletely assigned.

records.label: Methionine
records.limitation: Capacity admission only: no CoQ-specific intake target, rate limitation under adequate nutrition, increased synthesis from extra intake, mitochondrial delivery or clinical benefit is established.

records.label: Methionine
records.limitation: Endogenous remethylation also supplies methionine. Neonatal-piglet isotope incorporation does not establish an adult intake target, cerebral delivery or benefit above adequacy. Methyl allocation, SAH inhibition, transport and other substrate availability constrain the route; no shared KC admission follows.

records.label: CoQ10
records.limitation: Not an independent PM dietary admission. Food occurrence and endogenous biochemical participation remain valid distinct facts.

records.label: CoQ10
records.limitation: The existing coq10 identity and page resolve without a registry change. Ubiquinol is a reduced form, not an alias for oxidised ubiquinone. Dietary supply, endogenous synthesis, redox-form conversion and mitochondrial protective delivery remain separately assessed; no new dietary admission is established.

records.label: S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)
records.limitation: Not an independent PM dietary admission. Food occurrence and endogenous biochemical participation remain valid distinct facts.

records.label: Methionine-derived S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)
records.limitation: The dietary methionine route is assessed separately. This intracellular SAM participant is not a requirement to consume SAM supplements.

records.label: Flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD)
records.limitation: Not an independent PM dietary admission. Food occurrence and endogenous biochemical participation remain valid distinct facts.

records.label: Nicotinamide (a form of vitamin B3)
records.limitation: The review identifies the salvage substrate. It does not show that eating more nicotinamide, once intake is adequate, raises NAD⁺. The myopathy niacin study used nicotinic acid at pharmacological doses.

records.label: Nicotinic acid (a form of vitamin B3)
records.limitation: In five adults with mitochondrial myopathy, niacin at 750–1,000 mg/day raised blood NAD⁺ and brought muscle NAD⁺ to the control level. That is medical dosing in a deficiency disease, not a result for adequate everyday intake, and attention was not measured.

records.label: Tryptophan
records.limitation: Most cells outside the liver do not run the full route. The review does not establish what share of the NAD⁺ pool comes from tryptophan, and eating more protein is not shown to raise NAD⁺.

records.label: NAD+ (oxidised nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide)
records.limitation: This is a biochemical cofactor target, not an independent oral target admission or food-content claim.

records.label: Nicotinamide riboside
records.limitation: Supplemental NR chloride at 100–1000 mg is not an effective milk dose. Blood responses do not establish neuronal or mitochondrial NAD delivery, redox flux, superiority to adequate niacin or clinical benefit. Intestinal metabolism and tissue salvage can differ from the displayed intracellular NRK route; other NAD precursors remain alternatives.

records.label: Creatine
records.limitation: The brain also synthesises creatine, and exogenous exposure produces smaller and less consistent cerebral responses than skeletal-muscle responses.

records.label: Arginine
records.limitation: Capacity of the endogenous synthesis route is distinct from a claim that extra amino-acid intake raises cerebral creatine, phosphocreatine buffering or cognition. AGAT feedback, GAMT methyl supply, organ exchange and SLC6A8-mediated tissue transport constrain delivery. Human renal GAA production is not a measurement of brain synthesis flux; rat arginine infusion and glycine null responses are not oral human efficacy experiments.

records.label: Glycine
records.limitation: Capacity of the endogenous synthesis route is distinct from a claim that extra amino-acid intake raises cerebral creatine, phosphocreatine buffering or cognition. AGAT feedback, GAMT methyl supply, organ exchange and SLC6A8-mediated tissue transport constrain delivery. Human renal GAA production is not a measurement of brain synthesis flux; rat arginine infusion and glycine null responses are not oral human efficacy experiments.

records.label: Manganese
records.limitation: Legacy cofactor label retained; the cited source establishes PM4 source regulation, not manganese dietary effectiveness.

records.label: Manganese
records.limitation: Capacity is supported by protein biochemistry and mouse dietary manipulation; no general-population limitation, extra-intake benefit or human supplement dose is established.

records.label: Selenium
records.limitation: Legacy record preserved. This assessment did not establish PM4-specific dietary engagement; general clearance roles are not imported.

records.label: Selenium
records.limitation: The mitochondrial-isoform experiment is not a selenium intake study. Dietary selenium studies considered separately measured cytosolic/whole-tissue PHGPX; an isoform-specific supply chain remains under review.

records.label: Zinc
records.limitation: Legacy record preserved. This assessment did not establish PM4-specific dietary engagement; general clearance roles are not imported.

records.label: Vitamin E
records.limitation: Alpha-tocopherol predominates in the assessed experiments; the canonical Vitamin E class is broader. Deficiency correction and high-dose genetic rescue do not establish ordinary-food intervention equivalence, universal tissue dependence or benefit above adequacy.

records.label: Glutathione
records.limitation: Direct oral GSH, dietary amino-acid supply and local protective activity are not interchangeable. The ethanol model shows a precursor intervention can fail when transport is impaired.

records.label: Magnesium
records.limitation: Legacy magnesium candidate retained; OXPHOS participation alone does not establish membrane/protein protection.

records.label: Carnitine
records.limitation: Reaction participation is distinct from a dietary effect. Identity is reconciled; the separate Capacity admission does not establish benefit from extra intake, ordinary-food efficacy or equivalent effects of different carnitine formulations.

records.label: L-Carnitine
records.limitation: Functional dependency and food composition support Capacity, not a need to increase intake. Endogenous synthesis, tissue uptake and conservation also sustain the pool. The existing extracted carnitine/carbohydrate intervention is formulation-specific; meat or dairy effects on transport flux, brain function or ADHD are not established.

records.label: Acetoacetate
records.limitation: Biochemical participant retained without a new canonical dietary-supply admission. Canonical identity/food or endogenous-supply reconciliation is required; no food contains the downstream fuel by inference.

records.label: Caprylic Triglyceride
records.limitation: Uncontrolled sequential exposure: C8/C10 mixture (n=11) then 95% tricaprylin (n=6), 30 g/day for one month each. No claim of isolated C8 superiority, cognitive efficacy, healthy-person requirement or ordinary coconut-oil equivalence. PET uptake/metabolism is not a direct cellular ATP assay; no food-effective dose or fixed conversion yield is inferred.

records.label: Vitamin A
records.limitation: Conversion and response depend on vitamin A form, status, absorption, and host context; supplementation evidence is not a general dose-response claim for PM1.

records.label: Zinc
records.limitation: Direct requirement evidence is principally cellular and animal, with human supplementation evidence concentrated in deficiency or disease contexts; higher intake is not established to improve PM1 in zinc-sufficient people.

records.label: Zinc
records.limitation: Model-substrate chemistry, not ordinary dietary zinc limitation of human LPS containment. The enzyme’s ability to dephosphorylate critical lipid A groups depends on LPS structure.

records.label: Glutamine
records.limitation: Glutamine is supplied substantially from endogenous and systemic pools and becomes conditionally indispensable under stress; adult supplementation trials show no overall permeability benefit, so dietary protein or glutamine provision is not established as a general PM1 lever. A separate postinfectious IBS trial supports a selected supplementation response; this does not establish general need. The new Capacity assessment admits supply to junction-supporting cellular capacity, without asserting universal dietary limitation, benefit from extra intake, or equivalence to the supplemental exposure.

records.label: Glutamine for selected postinfectious IBS-D
records.limitation: 106 completers from115 randomised; narrative withdrawal counts are internally inconsistent. Use flow/Results cohort sizes, not a claim of complete intention-to-treat. Whey protein is not biologically inert; authors note possible IBS sensitivity. No significant symptom exacerbation was observed in control. Permeability was secondary; no direct junction-protein or mediator measurement. Not generalisable to IBS with normal permeability, other disease types, children, pregnancy/lactation or excluded renal/hepatic impairment. No significant control-arm permeability change; adverse-event rates similar and no serious adverse events reported. Long-term safety not established. Earlier discovery shorthand0.05 versus0.11 conflated post-treatment with active-group baseline; post-treatment control was0.10, and Table3 is the actual between-group change comparison.

records.label: FOS/GOS
records.limitation: Controlled human FOS/GOS fermentation does not establish the effects of inulin alone, individual FOS or GOS, ordinary food portions, or human tight-junction improvement.

records.label: Pectin
records.limitation: Human-faecal culture evidence is preparation-dependent and predominantly acetate-generating; it does not establish a uniform butyrate yield or human tight-junction benefit. Apple and citrus preparations are not interchangeable.

records.label: Citrus pectin
records.limitation: Defined-community mouse experiments and glycan assays do not establish equivalence across all pectins, a human intake target or beneficial host outcomes.

records.label: Pectin
records.limitation: Pectin structure, purified preparation, donor community and enriched culture medium affect interpretation. Pascale is secondary synthesis; Bang is bounded primary culture evidence. Whole apples are not equivalent to the tested citrus preparation; no human brain or clinical benefit is established.

records.label: Resistant starch
records.limitation: Response varies with starch type, preparation, dose and microbiota. Faecal short-chain fatty acids do not measure epithelial delivery or establish human tight-junction improvement; resistant potato starch results do not establish effects for every RS2 or RS3 preparation.

records.label: Resistant starch (RS2/RS3)
records.limitation: Cultures and one donor’s faecal rescue do not establish oral R. bromii efficacy, uniform human processing, equivalence to RS4 or clinical benefit.

records.label: Resistant starch
records.limitation: Utilisation and product distribution depend on starch structure, processing, accessibility, primary degraders and cross-feeding partners. Evidence for one formulation does not establish an equivalent butyrate response from another preparation or whole food. No predictable yield, intake target or brain benefit is established.

records.label: Oligofructose
records.limitation: The human result used 21 g/day for 12 weeks in 37 adults; it does not establish nutritional necessity, clinical benefit or equivalent effects from every food or fibre.

records.label: Magnesium
records.limitation: Purified calf enzyme and model substrates; magnesium effects differ for other reactions. This does not establish a dietary magnesium constraint on host endotoxin exposure.

records.label: Pea-fibre arabinan
records.limitation: Defined human-derived communities in mice; the food matrix and competitors affect access. No universal human response, optimal dose or host benefit is established.

records.label: Inulin
records.limitation: Utilisation genes, chain length, alternative substrates and resident organisms constrain the response. A supplied inulin substrate is not an indispensable intake, a guaranteed abundance shift, butyrate yield, mucus effect or clinical benefit.

records.label: Inulin
records.limitation: Culture conditions and community composition constrain production. Human inulin tracer estimates depend on assumed systemic availability; the human chicory-inulin trial did not significantly increase faecal butyrate. No fixed food yield, intake target or brain benefit is established.

records.label: Acetate
records.limitation: Endogenous microbial provision, absorption and compartmentation matter. Extra oral intake and benefit are not established by these studies.

records.label: Propionate

records.label: Butyrate

records.label: Ellagic acid
records.limitation: Conversion depends on microbial community and may stop at intermediates. This does not imply universal conversion, increased mitochondrial function or benefit.

records.label: Ellagitannins
records.limitation: The human study tested a pomegranate-juice matrix rather than isolated equivalence of every ellagitannin; final metabolite generation varies.

records.label: Epicatechin
records.limitation: Donor cultures do not establish a predictable whole-food conversion yield, mitochondrial effect or clinical benefit. Human apple-extract evidence involves mixed monomeric catechins, not isolated epicatechin efficacy. Do not generalise to EGCG or all procyanidins.

records.label: Glucose
records.limitation: Experimental neural response is not an optimal intake, an inadequacy threshold or benefit from more sugar.

records.label: Glutamate
records.limitation: This intracellular signalling role does not establish a requirement to eat glutamate or a human health benefit.

records.label: Linoleic acid
records.limitation: This is physiological nutrient sensing, not a beneficial direction or a need to increase linoleic acid. Human food-level circuit responses, vagal tone, ADHD and clinical benefits were not established. Foods generally supply esterified fatty acids released during digestion; the experimental free-fatty-acid stimulus is not a demonstrated food effect. More signalling is not automatically better.

records.label: Tryptophan
records.limitation: Substrate participation is not benefit from increased intake; host absorption, endogenous competition and microbial compartmentation differ from brain precursor delivery.

records.label: Pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP; active vitamin B6 cofactor)
records.limitation: Microbes can synthesise cofactors; this does not establish a host dietary vitamin B6 requirement or a beneficial direction of tryptophanase activity.

records.limitation: Dietary-depletion evidence is preclinical; extra intake in magnesium-replete humans is not shown here.

records.label: Resistant starch

records.label: DHA (Docosahexaenoic Acid)

It does not establish adipose secretion, receptor sensitivity, universal benefit, ordinary-food efficacy or a food-effective dose. Mixture and carrier effects are not attributed to DHA alone; DHA-specific attribution uses the separate DHA-versus-EPA trial.

records.label: Phosphatidylethanolamine
records.limitation: Intracellular phospholipid provision does not establish a requirement to consume NAPE or phosphatidylethanolamine.

records.label: Indispensable amino-acid supply
records.limitation: Protein-quality scoring and vegetarian-diet amino-acid coverage do not establish that increasing protein raises brain monoamine synthesis or improves attention or mood. The indispensable set includes phenylalanine; tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.

records.label: Tyrosine
records.limitation: Dietary supply to a circulating pool is distinct from brain transport, catecholamine synthesis or clinical benefit. A small human study found higher plasma tyrosine during protein-containing meals and after a large tyrosine supplement; it does not define ordinary-food efficacy or a need for extra tyrosine when supply is adequate. Tyrosine is not an indispensable amino acid.

records.label: Tryptophan
records.limitation: Pool presence of tryptophan is not evidence for increased brain serotonin, brain entry, or an attention or mood benefit.

records.label: Tyrosine
records.limitation: Competitive transport biology does not establish that eating more tyrosine increases brain tyrosine or catecholamine signalling.

records.label: Tryptophan
records.limitation: Meal-driven changes in plasma tryptophan-to-LNAA ratios do not establish increased brain serotonin or a clinical benefit.

records.label: Monoamine precursor supply
records.limitation: Only tyrosine supply is admitted here. Phenylalanine publication awaits its individual source/context appraisal; tryptophan is not admitted as catecholamine supply. Competitive inadequacy as a limiting constraint remains unresolved.

records.label: Methyl-resource supply for COMT
records.limitation: This establishes the connected biochemical supply route, not a measured dietary effect on regional neural SAM or COMT clearance. BHMT is predominantly hepatic/renal; peripheral methionine contribution, local SAM synthesis, alternative supply and turnover vary by tissue. Donor inadequacy as a limiting constraint and benefit from extra intake in replete individuals remain unresolved.

records.label: Iron
records.limitation: Human intake-to-dopamine responsiveness and clinical benefit were not established; the direct dopamine-metabolite evidence assessed here is preclinical deficiency evidence.

records.label: Pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP; active vitamin B6 cofactor)
records.limitation: Kennedy reviews B-vitamin roles in neurochemical synthesis; this does not establish dietary PLP provision or an intake-to-dopamine response in humans.

records.label: Vitamin B6
records.limitation: Dietary B6 can supply PLP precursors, including vitamers that enter the central nervous system, but increasing B6 intake has not been shown to increase human brain dopamine synthesis.

records.label: Tyrosine
records.limitation: Substrate necessity does not establish that additional dietary tyrosine increases brain dopamine or improves a functional or clinical outcome.

records.label: Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4)
records.limitation: BH4 is synthesised and recycled in vivo; this is not evidence for dietary BH4 provision or increased dopamine synthesis.

records.label: Vitamin B9 (folate)
records.limitation: This requires functional B12-dependent remethylation. The connected reaction chain does not measure dietary folate contribution to regional brain SAM or clearance; alternative methionine supply and tissue turnover matter. A limiting effect and benefit from extra intake remain unresolved.

records.label: Betaine
records.limitation: This is peripheral BHMT supply, not neuronal BHMT activity or measured delivery into neural SAM. Dietary methionine and folate remethylation provide alternatives. Homocysteine lowering does not establish regional clearance, a limiting constraint or benefit from extra intake.

records.label: Choline
records.limitation: Only choline-to-betaine methyl supply is admitted, not membrane or acetylcholine roles. Oxidation, peripheral BHMT, alternative methionine supply and local neural SAM turnover limit interpretation. Neural delivery, increased clearance, a limiting constraint and extra-intake benefit are not measured.

records.label: Phenylalanine
records.limitation: Human peripheral conversion supplies circulating tyrosine; neuronal delivery uses the separately supported transport chain. This does not establish increased dopamine/noradrenaline output, a limiting intake or benefit from extra phenylalanine. Hydroxylation, renal/hepatic function and LNAA competition matter; high phenylalanine is not interchangeable with tyrosine.

records.label: Phosphatidylcholine

records.label: Acetyl-CoA

records.label: Vitamin B5 (pantothenate)
records.limitation: Chronic ethanol-associated pantothenate depletion and rescue affected acetylcholine synthesis in rats; this does not establish that extra B5 raises brain acetylcholine in adequately nourished humans.

records.label: Vitamin B9 (folate)
records.limitation: Animal evidence is conditional on age, brain region and experimental context. Choline and acetylcholine concentrations were measured; methyl-dependent choline retention and the consequence for synthesis capacity are mechanistic inferences, not measured human synthesis flux. Folate is not a ChAT cofactor; extra folate above adequacy and cognitive benefit are not established.

records.label: Sodium
records.limitation: Transport-ion capacity does not establish that added dietary salt increases brain choline uptake or acetylcholine output. CNS homeostasis and membrane gradients intervene. Chloride is not assumed to have identical transport stoichiometry and is not independently admitted here.

records.label: Methyl-derived DHA-carrier supply
records.limitation: Supported biochemical supply chain, not a demonstrated increase in net adult brain DHA incorporation. Folate/choline compensation, hepatic BHMT, SAM turnover and carrier remodelling vary by context. Mouse folate effects were sex/tissue dependent; betaine rescue used ethanol-exposed rats. The downstream human tracer study administered choline, not folate or betaine. A donor-specific limiting effect and extra-intake benefit remain unresolved.

records.label: DHA
records.limitation: Diet can provide DHA for membrane incorporation. That does not establish an ADHD treatment effect or a human dosing rule from the porcine phospholipid comparison.

records.label: Choline
records.limitation: Human plasma isotopic enrichment is not absolute hepatic flux, net carrier supply or adult neuronal DHA incorporation. Higher choline intake did not increase total plasma LPC-DHA in the feeding study. The carrier-to-brain connection uses separate cell/mouse transport evidence. Donor inadequacy as a limiting constraint, compensation and benefit from extra intake remain unresolved.

records.label: Vitamin B9 (folate)

records.label: Betaine

records.label: Sodium
records.limitation: This supports the specific LPC-DHA carrier route, not all DHA delivery or direct neural incorporation from a meal. Sodium homeostasis, carrier formation and membrane gradients intervene; no added-salt recommendation, food-effective dose or clinical benefit.

records.label: Sodium
records.limitation: Established transport-ion capacity does not show that increasing dietary sodium increases brain clearance. CNS ion regulation and Na/K-pump energy supply intervene; transporter gradients are not inferred from a food quantity. No added-salt recommendation or clinical benefit.

records.label: Potassium
records.limitation: Established transport-ion capacity does not show that increasing dietary potassium increases brain clearance. CNS ion regulation and Na/K-pump energy supply intervene; transporter gradients are not inferred from a food quantity. No added-salt recommendation or clinical benefit.

records.label: Magnesium
records.limitation: Neuronal ion-manipulation experiments establish physiological capacity, not oral magnesium delivery at a pharmacological concentration, treatment of excitotoxic injury or benefit above adequacy. Brain homeostasis and membrane voltage remain determinants; more NMDA inhibition is not automatically beneficial.

records.label: Glutamate
records.limitation: The evidence establishes glutamate as the GAD substrate, not that dietary glutamate or protein controls neuronal glutamate availability or human brain GABA synthesis.

records.label: Pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP; active vitamin B6 cofactor)
records.limitation: The evidence establishes PLP dependence of GAD, but not dietary PLP provision or an intake-to-synthesis response in humans.

records.label: Vitamin B6
records.limitation: Dietary B6 provision of PLP precursors is supported, but increasing B6 intake has not been shown to increase human brain GABA synthesis; PLP supports many enzymes and is not GABA-specific.

records.label: Choline
records.limitation: This is membrane-precursor provision through the Kennedy route. Choline was not isolated in the gerbil spine experiment; no increased human synapse number or benefit from extra intake is established.

records.label: Uridine
records.limitation: Endogenous nucleotide synthesis and salvage also contribute. UMP alone did not significantly increase gerbil spine density; that null structural result does not erase the precursor role. No ordinary-food dose or human structural benefit is established.

records.label: Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)
records.limitation: This is a preclinical structural state response, not proof of an indispensable intake or verified new synapse counts. It does not establish human synapse growth, ordinary-food equivalence or cognitive benefit. Developmental mouse marker and visual-response evidence is additional, context-specific support; marker abundance is not an ultrastructurally verified contact count.

records.label: 5-Methyltetrahydrofolate
records.limitation: Necessity of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate does not show that raising its intake increases tissue methionine-synthase flux.

records.label: Vitamin B9 (folate)
records.limitation: This conversion pathway does not show that increasing folate intake increases tissue remethylation flux. Folic acid lowers blood homocysteine, which is a circulating marker.

records.label: Methylcobalamin
records.limitation: Cofactor necessity does not show that extra vitamin B12 increases tissue methionine-synthase flux when stores are already adequate.

records.label: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin)
records.limitation: Provision of vitamin B12 does not show that increasing intake raises tissue remethylation flux. Added vitamin B12 further lowered blood homocysteine beyond folic acid in pooled trials, which remains a circulating marker.

records.label: Homocysteine
records.limitation: Homocysteine is produced inside the methionine cycle. It is not a dietary requirement of this reaction, and methionine, the product, is not a dietary input for it.

records.label: Flavin adenine dinucleotide
records.limitation: This is a biochemical cofactor target, not an independent oral FAD admission or food-content claim.

records.label: Vitamin B2
records.limitation: Foundational human-enzyme cofactor provenance supports capacity; it is not a measurement of dietary riboflavin-induced remethylation flux, brain methylation or benefit above adequacy. FMN is also required; FAD is the endpoint of the displayed activation chain, not its sole functional cofactor.

records.label: Betaine
records.limitation: Supplemental betaine lowers plasma homocysteine in healthy adults, but that change does not measure tissue BHMT activity or show a clinical benefit. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved.

records.label: Choline
records.limitation: Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved.

records.label: Homocysteine
records.limitation: Homocysteine is produced in the methionine cycle and is not a dietary input for this reaction.

records.label: Zinc
records.limitation: Human purified-enzyme metal removal/reconstitution and ligand mutants establish zinc-dependent capacity. Dietary zinc supplies the same element, but no human extra-intake BHMT flux response, intake threshold or cognitive benefit is established.

records.label: One-carbon methyl-donor pool (folate, betaine, choline)
records.limitation: Deficiency and pathway-impairment studies support this upstream connection, with responses varying by tissue and condition. KC1’s limiting effect on MAT-dependent synthesis remains unresolved; SAMe abundance also reflects consumption and turnover. Benefit from additional intake in nutrient-replete individuals is not established. This pool relationship is distinct from PM3’s biochemical reaction requirements.

records.label: Methionine
records.limitation: No ordinary-diet human dose-response demonstrating increased MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis was identified.

records.label: ATP
records.limitation: Diet does not supply ATP to MAT; no dietary ATP lever for SAMe synthesis is established.

records.label: Magnesium
records.limitation: Human MAT structural and enzymological evidence establishes catalytic capacity. Ordinary food supply is distinct from measured MAT flux; no benefit from additional magnesium in replete people or universal methylation increase is asserted.

records.label: Potassium
records.limitation: Human MAT structures establish the specific ion relationship. Physiological potassium homeostasis and tissue uptake intervene; no claim that extra dietary potassium raises SAM flux or improves methylation is established.

records.label: Dietary protein
records.limitation: Dietary protein provides digestible methionine, but this does not establish that increasing protein or methionine intake increases MAT-dependent SAMe synthesis in humans. DIAAS evaluates sulfur amino acids as methionine + cysteine.

records.label: Vitamin B9 (folate)
records.limitation: This is upstream methionine supply, not a MAT substrate or cofactor. The route depends on functional vitamin B12-dependent methionine synthase; alternative methionine supply and tissue context affect its contribution. Increased MAT flux or benefit from extra folate in replete individuals is not established.

records.label: Betaine
records.limitation: BHMT activity is concentrated mainly in liver and kidney; this is not local BHMT activity in every tissue. Folate-dependent remethylation and dietary methionine provide alternative supply. Homocysteine lowering does not establish increased MAT flux, increased SAMe availability or benefit from extra intake in replete individuals.

records.label: Choline
records.limitation: Only the choline-to-betaine methyl-supply route is admitted here, not choline membrane or neurotransmitter roles. Oxidation, predominantly hepatic/renal BHMT activity and alternative supply constrain interpretation. Increased MAT flux, increased SAMe availability or benefit from additional choline in replete individuals is not established.

records.label: One-carbon methyl-donor pool (folate, betaine, choline)
records.limitation: BHMT is mainly hepatic/renal and alternative methionine supply can compensate. The supported routes do not show that donor availability limits net cycle rates or the remethylation–transsulfuration split. Homocysteine concentration is not branch flux.

records.label: Methionine
records.limitation: Methionine is required to enter the cycle. This does not show that raising methionine intake increases human remethylation or transsulfuration rates.

records.label: Dietary protein
records.limitation: Dietary protein supplies methionine. It does not show that eating more protein increases cycle rates. DIAAS scores sulfur amino acids as methionine plus cysteine.

records.label: Vitamin B9 (folate)
records.limitation: Folic acid can lower blood homocysteine concentration. That concentration change is not a measured change in remethylation or transsulfuration rate.

records.label: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin)
records.limitation: Added vitamin B12 can lower blood homocysteine further after folic acid. That is a concentration result, not a measured cycle-rate response.

records.label: Vitamin B6
records.limitation: In nine healthy young adults, 28 days of vitamin B6 restriction lowered plasma pyridoxal phosphate and did not change mean postprandial remethylation, transmethylation, or total transsulfuration rates.

records.label: Vitamin B2 (riboflavin)
records.limitation: Riboflavin supports formation of the methyl donor. It is not the cofactor at the methionine-synthase catalytic site, and it has not been shown to change human cycle rates.

records.label: Betaine
records.limitation: BHMT activity is concentrated mainly in liver and kidney; this is not local BHMT activity in every tissue. Folate-dependent remethylation and dietary methionine provide alternative supply. Homocysteine lowering does not establish increased MAT flux, increased SAMe availability or benefit from extra intake in replete individuals.

records.label: Choline
records.limitation: Only the choline-to-betaine methyl-supply route is admitted here, not choline membrane or neurotransmitter roles. Oxidation, predominantly hepatic/renal BHMT activity and alternative supply constrain interpretation. Increased integrated cycle flux or improved branch balance or benefit from additional choline in replete individuals is not established.

records.label: Glycine
records.limitation: Endogenous glycine synthesis and other methyltransferases also contribute. Enzyme loss is not glycine deficiency; extra dietary glycine has not been established to normalise whole-cycle or brain methylation.

records.label: Methionine-cycle sulfur supply
records.limitation: Supported upstream supply, not direct CBS substrate or established sulfur-pool limitation. Cysteine is the product of this PM and is not admitted as an additional supply input. Tissue allocation, compensation and benefit from extra methionine intake are not established.

records.label: Combined folate/choline donor availability
records.limitation: Four-week combined folate/choline deprivation in male rats on a 20% casein formula with antibiotic suppression of microbial folate synthesis. Extracted liver CBS activity, not in-vivo flux or brain activity, was measured. Neither constituent alone significantly reduced CBS activity in this experiment. SAM mediation is supported mechanistically but was not isolated causally; liver lipid changes accompanied deprivation. This does not establish extra-intake benefit, betaine deficiency or uniform donor limitation.

records.label: Pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP; active vitamin B6 cofactor)
records.limitation: Purified-enzyme dependence on pyridoxal 5'-phosphate does not show that raising vitamin B6 intake increases cysteine formation in people. Moderate B6 restriction changed cystathionine handling but did not significantly reduce total transsulfuration in the assessed human tracer study.

records.label: Vitamin B6
records.limitation: Salvage of food vitamin B6 to pyridoxal 5'-phosphate does not show that higher vitamin B6 intake increases cystathionine beta-synthase or cystathionine gamma-lyase flux. Moderate B6 restriction changed cystathionine handling but did not significantly reduce total transsulfuration in the assessed human tracer study.

records.label: Homocysteine
records.limitation: Homocysteine is generated inside one-carbon metabolism. It is not a dietary intake, and its use by cystathionine beta-synthase does not show that diet controls transsulfuration flux.

records.label: Serine
records.limitation: Serine is a direct enzyme substrate. Endogenous synthesis and diet can both supply it; this does not show that dietary serine or protein intake increases cystathionine formation.

records.label: Cystathionine
records.limitation: Cystathionine is formed inside this pathway. It is not a dietary intake, and its cleavage does not measure whole-body transsulfuration flux.

records.label: Methionine
records.limitation: Supported upstream supply, not direct CBS substrate or established sulfur-pool limitation. Cysteine is the product of this PM and is not admitted as an additional supply input. Tissue allocation, compensation and benefit from extra methionine intake are not established.

records.label: Cysteine
records.limitation: Cysteine is the substrate of the first assembly step. A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, and that formula also removed methionine. When methionine intake stayed adequate, removing cysteine did not lower red-cell synthesis in young men. This does not show that eating more cysteine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis.

records.label: Glutamate
records.limitation: No human study in this assessment showed that changing dietary glutamate changes glutathione synthesis.

records.label: Glycine
records.limitation: In older adults glycine was supplemented together with a cysteine precursor, so that rise in erythrocyte synthesis does not isolate glycine.

records.label: ATP
records.limitation: Diet does not supply ATP to these enzymes, and no dietary ATP lever is established.

records.label: Magnesium
records.limitation: Human GSS crystallography and cofactor annotation support capacity. The structure contains two magnesium ions; this does not establish a dietary dose, increased blood or neuronal glutathione synthesis, or benefit above adequacy. Original one-per-subunit wording is retained in history rather than used as dietary stoichiometry.

records.label: Methionine
records.limitation: A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, so that result does not isolate methionine. In the cysteine-free study, methionine intake stayed adequate and red-cell synthesis did not fall. This does not show that eating more methionine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis.

records.label: N-acetylcysteine
records.limitation: The synthesis increase was measured in older adults given this precursor together with glycine. It does not show an effect of N-acetylcysteine alone, of ordinary foods, or of supplementation outside that group, and it is not a neuronal or clinical result.

records.label: One-carbon methyl-donor availability
records.limitation: Conditional animal evidence; tracer enrichment is not absolute flux. No universal donor limitation, human intake target or cognitive benefit is established.

records.label: Vitamin B9 (folate)
records.limitation: The response was conditional on sex and experimental context. Methyl-derived PC enrichment is not absolute PEMT flux; extra folate above adequacy is not established to enhance formation or cognition.

records.label: Betaine
records.limitation: Abstract-level rescue evidence under ethanol-induced imbalance does not establish ordinary betaine deficiency, universal intake responsiveness or cognitive benefit; full assay methods remain unavailable.

records.label: Phosphatidylethanolamine
records.limitation: This identifies the phospholipid substrate of the reaction. It does not show that eating phosphatidylethanolamine or ethanolamine increases hepatic PEMT activity in humans.

records.label: S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe)
records.limitation: SAMe is made for this reaction by methionine adenosyltransferase. Needing SAMe as a substrate does not make SAMe supplements a requirement of the methylation, and it does not show that raising SAMe intake increases PEMT activity in humans.

records.label: Choline
records.limitation: Plasma tracing does not measure absolute hepatic flux, intermediary SAM, ordinary-food equivalence or benefit.

records.label: Phosphatidylcholine
records.limitation: Plasma tracing does not measure absolute hepatic flux, intermediary SAM, ordinary-food equivalence or benefit.

records.label: Uridine
records.limitation: Uridine is a supported precursor source, not an indispensable dietary requirement: endogenous nucleotide synthesis and salvage also supply CTP. Rat-slice and oral-UMP gerbil results do not establish an ordinary-food dose, increased human PC flux or cognitive benefit; human MRS measures precursor pools.

records.label: Cytidine triphosphate (CTP)
records.limitation: This intracellular reaction participant is not a requirement to consume CTP. Nucleotide synthesis and salvage can supply it; more precursor does not establish greater human PC flux.

records.label: Diacylglycerol (DAG)
records.limitation: DAG is an intracellular substrate pool with varied fatty-acid composition, not a dietary DAG target or a DHA-specific requirement.

records.label: Choline
records.limitation: This reaction role is separate from choline methyl-donor provision to PEMT. It does not establish that extra choline increases brain PC synthesis.

records.label: Methionine
records.limitation: Endogenous remethylation also supplies methionine. Neonatal-piglet isotope incorporation does not establish an adult intake target, cerebral delivery or benefit above adequacy. Methyl allocation, SAH inhibition, transport and other substrate availability constrain the route; no shared KC admission follows.

records.label: Glutathione precursor pool (cysteine and glycine)
records.limitation: This is supported upstream supply, not a demonstrated dietary constraint on NF-κB. Human precursor supplementation measured red-cell glutathione, not NF-κB; cysteine was supplied as N-acetylcysteine together with glycine. Cellular redox studies show context-dependent effects, including inhibition after glutathione depletion or increased extracellular cysteine. Neither individual dietary limitation, brain transfer nor benefit from additional intake is established.

records.label: Magnesium ions (Mg²⁺)
records.limitation: Reviewed UniProt IKBKB records the ATP-dependent IκB kinase reaction without a magnesium cofactor annotation; published IKKβ crystals used in this review are inhibitor-bound rather than ATP–Mg ternary complexes. This does not establish that ordinary dietary magnesium intake limits human NF-κB transcription.

records.label: Oligofructose
records.limitation: Defined 10% w/w mouse feeding is not a human dose or an ordinary-food effect. This is state regulation, not indispensability. Oligofructose is not chemically converted into GLP-2; no isolated butyrate mediation, generic fibre effect or brain benefit is established.

records.label: Sulforaphane
records.limitation: Human target engagement varies by formulation, tissue and population. The positive study used a myrosinase-completed broccoli sprout homogenate for three days in healthy nonsmokers and measured nasal phase II enzyme RNA, not Nrf2 protein or nuclear translocation. Extract capsules did not increase lung target-gene expression in COPD. An ordinary broccoli meal, direct activation of Nrf2 in the human brain and clinical ADHD benefit remain unestablished. Sulforaphane is not an essential nutrient.

records.label: Selenium
records.limitation: In selenium-deficient adults, plasma glutathione peroxidase activity levelled off once intake reached about 35 micrograms a day. Intake above that plateau did not raise the enzyme further, and the study did not measure net oxidative pressure.

records.label: Zinc
records.limitation: Curated human SOD1 and experimental structural evidence support a structural capacity relationship, not zinc-dependent catalysis identical to copper. Human dietary SOD responses vary by isoform and status; extra zinc can disturb copper availability. No general oxidative-stress improvement or benefit above adequacy is established.

records.label: Copper
records.limitation: Erythrocyte superoxide dismutase rose after copper repletion in infants with marginal copper status. That does not show that extra copper raises the enzyme when status is already adequate.

records.label: Manganese
records.limitation: Human SOD2 requires manganese; dietary depletion experiments measured lower heart and kidney MnSOD activity in rats. This establishes a bounded enzyme-capacity dependency, not a human dose recommendation, universal tissue response, measured net ROS balance or benefit above adequate intake.

records.label: Glutathione
records.limitation: Glutathione is made in the body and used by the peroxidase. That is not evidence for eating glutathione.

records.label: Iron
records.limitation: Rat diet and tissue context; the kidney result is not a uniform response across organs or a human intake threshold. Human catalase haem identity supports capacity, not benefit from extra iron. Iron can also promote non-enzymatic oxidation; higher catalase activity is not a clinical benefit.

records.label: Vitamin E
records.limitation: Vitamin E breaks peroxyl-radical chains in membranes. That chemistry does not show that extra vitamin E lowers peroxidation in people. A prevention trial found more prostate cancers with 400 IU a day.

records.label: Selenium
records.limitation: Mouse whole-organ enzyme assays do not identify mitochondrial isoforms, a human food dose or benefit above selenium adequacy. Repletion response depended on dose; antioxidant capacity does not establish clinical prevention.

records.label: Vitamin C
records.limitation: Pulse radiolysis shows ascorbate reacting with the vitamin E radical. It does not show that more vitamin C speeds recycling in people.

records.label: Vitamin E
records.limitation: Regeneration of the vitamin E radical is not a high-dose rule. A prevention trial found more prostate cancers with 400 IU of vitamin E a day.

records.label: Vitamin B2
records.limitation: Human red-cell enzyme evidence supports flavin-dependent capacity. It does not establish neuronal or whole-body recycling flux, benefit above adequacy, or equivalence between an ordinary food and a 5 mg/day supplement.

records.label: Flavin adenine dinucleotide
records.limitation: Reaction participation does not establish oral FAD delivery, a food FAD concentration or additional-intake benefit.

records.label: Selenium
records.limitation: Culture selenium exposure is not an oral food dose. This supports the thioredoxin arm, not selenium dependence of glutathione reductase, universal tissue recycling flux or benefit above adequacy.

records.label: DHA (Docosahexaenoic Acid)
records.limitation: Fifteen male soccer players, eight weeks, 1.16 g DHA/day in a matched beverage comparison. Ex-vivo stimulated production is not resting circulating signalling, receptor response or universal anti-inflammatory benefit. No effect from ordinary fish portions or brain/ADHD outcome is established; temperature and exercise responses differ.

records.label: EPA
records.limitation: Five days of 2.4 g a day in healthy adults raised some pro-resolving mediators, not every mediator, and not a disease-resolution outcome.

records.label: DHA
records.limitation: Five days of 2.4 g a day in healthy adults raised some pro-resolving mediators, not every mediator, and not a disease-resolution outcome.

records.label: Iron
records.limitation: This identifies iron centres in the chain. It does not show that eating more iron, once iron status is adequate, raises electron transport.

records.label: Flavin mononucleotide (FMN)
records.limitation: The review identifies the cofactor. It does not show that flavin mononucleotide (FMN) supply limits complex I in ordinary life, or that raising intake increases electron transport.

records.label: Vitamin B2 (riboflavin)
records.limitation: The review does not show that eating more riboflavin, once flavin mononucleotide (FMN) is adequate, raises electron transport. Riboflavin-responsive complex I disease is a separate clinical context.

records.label: Ubiquinone
records.limitation: Cells synthesise ubiquinone. These reviews do not show that dietary coenzyme Q10 raises electron transport.

records.label: Copper
records.limitation: Specific complex-IV metal dependence and dietary-deficiency evidence support capacity supply. Rat cardiac protein/activity effects are not a human optimisation dose, a universal tissue response or proof that extra copper improves electron transport when status is adequate.

records.label: Tyrosine
records.limitation: Capacity admission only: no CoQ-specific intake target, rate limitation under adequate nutrition, increased synthesis from extra intake, mitochondrial delivery or clinical benefit is established. Endogenous phenylalanine conversion is an alternative source; the full human intervening enzyme sequence remains incompletely assigned.

records.label: Methionine
records.limitation: Capacity admission only: no CoQ-specific intake target, rate limitation under adequate nutrition, increased synthesis from extra intake, mitochondrial delivery or clinical benefit is established.

records.limitation: Capacity admission only: no CoQ-specific intake target, rate limitation under adequate nutrition, increased synthesis from extra intake, mitochondrial delivery or clinical benefit is established.

records.limitation: Capacity admission only: no CoQ-specific intake target, rate limitation under adequate nutrition, increased synthesis from extra intake, mitochondrial delivery or clinical benefit is established.

records.label: CoQ10
records.limitation: Not an independent PM dietary admission. Food occurrence and endogenous biochemical participation remain valid distinct facts.

records.label: S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)
records.limitation: Not an independent PM dietary admission. Food occurrence and endogenous biochemical participation remain valid distinct facts.

records.label: Flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD)
records.limitation: Not an independent PM dietary admission. Food occurrence and endogenous biochemical participation remain valid distinct facts.

records.label: Nicotinamide (a form of vitamin B3)
records.limitation: The review identifies the salvage substrate. It does not show that eating more nicotinamide, once intake is adequate, raises NAD⁺. The myopathy niacin study used nicotinic acid at pharmacological doses.

records.label: Nicotinic acid (a form of vitamin B3)
records.limitation: In five adults with mitochondrial myopathy, niacin at 750–1,000 mg/day raised blood NAD⁺ and brought muscle NAD⁺ to the control level. That is medical dosing in a deficiency disease, not a result for adequate everyday intake, and attention was not measured.

records.label: Tryptophan
records.limitation: Most cells outside the liver do not run the full route. The review does not establish what share of the NAD⁺ pool comes from tryptophan, and eating more protein is not shown to raise NAD⁺.

records.label: NAD+ (oxidised nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide)
records.limitation: This is a biochemical cofactor target, not an independent oral target admission or food-content claim.

records.label: Nicotinamide riboside
records.limitation: Supplemental NR chloride at 100–1000 mg is not an effective milk dose. Blood responses do not establish neuronal or mitochondrial NAD delivery, redox flux, superiority to adequate niacin or clinical benefit. Intestinal metabolism and tissue salvage can differ from the displayed intracellular NRK route; other NAD precursors remain alternatives.

records.label: Creatine
records.limitation: The brain also synthesises creatine, and exogenous exposure produces smaller and less consistent cerebral responses than skeletal-muscle responses.

records.label: Arginine
records.limitation: Capacity of the endogenous synthesis route is distinct from a claim that extra amino-acid intake raises cerebral creatine, phosphocreatine buffering or cognition. AGAT feedback, GAMT methyl supply, organ exchange and SLC6A8-mediated tissue transport constrain delivery. Human renal GAA production is not a measurement of brain synthesis flux; rat arginine infusion and glycine null responses are not oral human efficacy experiments.

records.label: Glycine
records.limitation: Capacity of the endogenous synthesis route is distinct from a claim that extra amino-acid intake raises cerebral creatine, phosphocreatine buffering or cognition. AGAT feedback, GAMT methyl supply, organ exchange and SLC6A8-mediated tissue transport constrain delivery. Human renal GAA production is not a measurement of brain synthesis flux; rat arginine infusion and glycine null responses are not oral human efficacy experiments.

records.label: Methionine-derived S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)
records.limitation: The dietary methionine route is assessed separately. This intracellular SAM participant is not a requirement to consume SAM supplements.

records.limitation: Capacity is supported by protein biochemistry and mouse dietary manipulation; no general-population limitation, extra-intake benefit or human supplement dose is established.

records.limitation: The existing coq10 identity and page resolve without a registry change. Ubiquinol is a reduced form, not an alias for oxidised ubiquinone.
